request: Analyze GSE246428 for PMID 39056292 (SPAG7 deletion causes intrauterine growth restriction, resulting in adulthood obesity and metabolic dysfunction.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (polyA, NovaSeq 2x150), gastrocnemius muscle, 28-week-old female mice (S4.17.p1, S4.18.p1, S4.1.p2)
final.sample_inclusion: WT and SPAG7 KO gastrocnemius; Fig 3K legend says n=7; two samples removed for a batch effect and a label mismatch (S4.19.p1); GEO deposits 9 samples (5 WT, 4 KO)
final.primary_estimand: genotype effect (SPAG7 KO vs WT) on sedentary gastrocnemius transcriptome; no exercise intervention in the sequenced samples. Exercise appears only as a phenotype readout (treadmill endurance test, S2.3.p1, S4.12.p1) and no exercised animals were sequenced
planned_contrasts: SPAG7 KO vs WT gastrocnemius (S2.3.p2; paper: 1,848 up / 2,291 down = 4,139 DEGs)
final.normalization: Salmon -> tximport gene-level counts rounded to integers (S4.19.p1; GEO data_processing)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 v1.34.0 (~ genotype implied); apeglm shrinkage for GSEA; clusterProfiler ORA/GSEA (S4.19.p1)

paper_threshold.source_locator: S2.3.p2 says 'significantly' without a stated rule; S4.19.p1 states no cutoff

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: The only sequencing dataset (DA.p1 -> GSE246428) is gastrocnemius RNA-seq from WT vs germline SPAG7 KO females (S4.17.p1, Fig 3K). The paper's exercise content is a treadmill endurance test used as a functional readout (S2.3.p1, S4.12.p1, Fig 3A-B); no exercise-trained or acutely exercised group was sequenced. The DEG threshold is not stated.

checks: GEO source/tissue = gastrocnemius muscle, Mus musculus, matches S4.17.p1
GEO data_processing (STAR/Salmon, GRCm39 Ens106, tximport rounded, DESeq2 v1.34.0) matches S4.19.p1
genotype WT/Spag7 KO matches the paper's RNA-seq contrast

ownership.reasoning: Series is cited in the data availability statement and its processing text matches the methods verbatim.

alignment.reasoning: Raw-count matrix columns (X2..X10) equal the metadata 'description' field exactly for all 9 samples (inspect alignment_keys: 9/9). Genotype is the only grouping column.

matrix.reasoning: GSE246428_Spag7_raw_counts.txt.gz is 100% integer; GEO data_processing states tximport gene-level estimates 'rounded to the nearest integer'; paper used DESeq2 on these (S4.19.p1). The other file holds DESeq2-normalized counts plus the authors' DE results and is not an input matrix.

candidates.reason_rejected: DESeq2-normalized counts mixed with authors' DE result columns; not raw input

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: every sequenced sample is a sedentary gastrocnemius from WT or SPAG7 KO mice (only factor genotype, 5 WT / 4 KO). The paper's exercise data are treadmill endurance phenotypes (S2.3.p1, S4.12.p1), not sequenced conditions, so an exercise effect on gene expression cannot be identified. Relabelling the KO-vs-WT genotype contrast as an exercise effect would change the estimand.
design.reasoning: The request asks how exercise affects gene expression. GEO metadata has one grouping column (genotype) and the paper's RNA-seq estimand is KO vs WT (S2.3.p2). KO mice have reduced exercise capacity, but that is a genotype phenotype, not an exercise intervention.

candidates.value: genotype KO vs WT as exercise proxy
candidates.reason_rejected: genetic knockout, not exercise; different estimand

discrepancies.paper: Fig 3K legend n=7; two samples removed (batch effect, label mismatch) per S4.19.p1
discrepancies.data: GEO deposits 9 samples (5 WT, 4 KO); removed samples not identified
